captive_summary: Grid-fed. Guanghui Energy built a dedicated 110kV substation specifically for this terminal's LNG-gasification/external-transmission works ('广汇能源LNG分销转运站LNG气化外输及其配套工程110kV变电所工程' — an EIA-registered project in its own right), and the terminal's vaporization process draws heat FROM an adjacent (unrelated) power plant's warm seawater rather than generating its own power. No on-site gas generation equipment found in any source.
confirmed_how: Jiangsu environmental-consulting firm's project listing (jsgh.com.cn) names the formal EIA project title '广汇能源LNG分销转运站LNG气化外输及其配套工程110kV变电所工程' — i.e. the terminal's electrical supply is a dedicated 110kV grid substation built as supporting infrastructure for gasification/export, not an on-site generator. Separately, a Tencent News (news.qq.com) report on the site's seawater-heat-recovery project states directly: '该项目利用邻近电厂温海水余热将LNG气化成天然气进行高压外输，降温后的冷海水排回电厂循环水前池继续使用' (the project uses warm seawater waste heat from the NEIGHBORING power plant to gasify the LNG, and the cooled seawater is returned to that plant) — confirming heat flows INTO the terminal from an external, unrelated power plant (process heat, not captive power, and not this terminal's own generation).

verification_log.note: Confirms EIA project title naming a 110kV substation built as part of the terminal's gasification/export works.
Confirms the terminal draws waste heat FROM an adjacent power plant (direction: heat IN, not captive generation).
